learning_objectives: Tell published guild claims, observable data, open allegations and later-established facts apart.
Read a few ledger lines without confusing sales, earnings, coin flow, debt and net owners' claim.
Explain concentration risk and how uncertainty should affect how much you commit.
See why a leadership change and unusual bookkeeping call for inquiry, without treating them as proof of wrongdoing.
State a decision, your evidence, the downside and a testable forecast before the future is shown.
Judge the quality of a decision separately from its result.

world.tone_notes: Rain on stained glass, gilded banners, a mystery to investigate. Income is not cash; a write-down is not a monster attack.

evidence.title: A High Master Steps Down
evidence.player_text: A proclamation is nailed to the Grand Exchange board. The high master of the Golden Guild Trading Consortium is stepping down. The council states the reason is personal, and the guild council chair will take over his duties.
evidence.teaching_note: Separate the observed event, a resignation, from the explanation offered by the guild. The stated reason is the guild's own words, not an established cause.

evidence.title: The Chair Speaks of Strength
evidence.player_text: In the tavern the talk turns to the council chair's words: he says the consortium is strong and its growth is bright. That is the chair's opinion of the guild, offered by the guild itself.
evidence.teaching_note: Management confidence is an opinion, not evidence of future results.

evidence.title: Questions Worth Asking
evidence.player_text: A well-worn checklist is passed around the tavern. Which part of the proclamation is an event that happened? Which part is an explanation given by the guild? What would an independent witness be able to confirm?
evidence.teaching_note: Source-comparison checklist unlocked by the Insight check; the same comparison is available freely by asking the scholar.

evidence.title: A Scribe's Margin Note on Deposits
evidence.player_text: A scribe's note beside the ledger explains that collateral placed with trading partners is counted inside the treasury movement register, so a drain there can reverse when the collateral returns.
evidence.teaching_note: Pre-authored explanation unlocked by the Investigation check; the side-by-side reconciliation is available freely in the quarterly ledger.

evidence.title: A Handbill from the Crowd
evidence.player_text: A handbill passed around the Grand Exchange says: everyone is buying ownership certificates of the Golden Guild, so how could it be wrong? Ren Tal calls this a mood, not a measurement.
evidence.teaching_note: Popularity is not evidence. Would you choose the same if this were your entire savings?

evidence.title: Mood at the Exchange
evidence.player_text: Broker Ren Tal says traders at the Grand Exchange feel uneasy about the high master's exit but still hopeful about the guild. He labels this his opinion of the crowd's mood, and promises nothing about prices.
evidence.teaching_note: Sentiment is an opinion about behavior, not a forecast or proof.

evidence.player_text: A new proclamation announces that the guild recorded a net loss of {FIG-Q3-LOSS} for the latest quarter, a loss of {FIG-Q3-EPS:abs} per ownership certificate.

evidence.title: A New Proclamation: The Valuation Corrections
evidence.player_text: The guild also announces valuation corrections to its assets worth {FIG-Q3-CHARGE} after tax. By its own account these include {FIG-Q3-C1} at a far-off waterworks venture, {FIG-Q3-C2} restructuring a signal-tower venture, and {FIG-Q3-C3} in losses on other investments and structured dealings.

evidence.teaching_note: The corrections are contained within the quarterly loss, not added on top. They are the guild's own classifications, not proof that the accounts are fully explained.

evidence.title: A New Proclamation: The Owners' Claim Shrinks
evidence.player_text: On the guild's results call it was said that the net owners' claim will be reduced by {FIG-Q3-EQ-CUT}.

figures.label: Reduction to the net owners' claim

evidence.teaching_note: A balance-sheet adjustment. It is not a coin payment and not a separate profit-and-loss charge.

evidence.title: The Guild Stresses Its Recurring Earnings
evidence.player_text: In the same proclamation the guild highlights {FIG-Q3-RECUR} of recurring earnings, or {FIG-Q3-RECUR-EPS} per ownership certificate, set against the overall loss.

figures.label: Recurring earnings

figures.label: Recurring earnings per ownership certificate
figures.period: the latest guild quarter

evidence.teaching_note: Reported recurring earnings do not erase the actual net loss. Compare what is emphasized with what is reported overall.

evidence.title: A Scholar's Gloss on Write-Downs
evidence.player_text: A scholar's gloss explains that a valuation correction lowers the recorded worth of an asset; it is an accounting entry, not a purse of coin leaving the treasury. Whether the underlying accounts are right is a separate question.
evidence.teaching_note: Approved explanation unlocked by the Investigation check; Buddy and the scholar offer the same lesson freely.

evidence.title: The Exchange Reacts
evidence.player_text: Broker Ren Tal says the Grand Exchange is rattled by the heavy loss and the shrinking owners' claim. He calls this his reading of the crowd, and guarantees nothing about where prices go next.

encounters.title: The Resignation
encounters.failure_forward: Compare the two passages of the proclamation side by side, or ask the scholar; no essential evidence is lost.
encounters.teaching_target: The difference between an observed event and an explanation offered by the guild.

encounters.title: The Quarterly Ledger
encounters.failure_forward: The statement reconciliation is placed side by side with the earnings ledger; nothing is hidden behind the dice.
encounters.teaching_target: Separating reported earnings from coin movement and borrowed funds.

encounters.title: The New Loss Report
encounters.failure_forward: Buddy walks through the terms, and the treasurer and scholar can be asked further questions.
encounters.teaching_target: How genuinely new public evidence should update beliefs and capital allocation.

encounters.title: The Crowd at the Exchange
encounters.failure_forward: A shorter, plainer exchange with the broker; the roll cannot create a new financial fact.
encounters.teaching_target: Distinguishing evidence from popularity, and managing concentration risk.

news.headline: The Golden Guild Reports a Heavy Loss
news.summary: A new proclamation tells of a net loss of {FIG-Q3-LOSS}, valuation corrections of {FIG-Q3-CHARGE} after tax, and a smaller net owners' claim. The guild stresses {FIG-Q3-RECUR} of recurring earnings alongside it.

questions: What was knowable when you committed?
Which concerns were evident then, and which only became public afterward?
Did your analysis distinguish managerial claims from independent evidence?
Would diversifying or holding some cash have changed your exposure?
Did you succeed because of the process, luck, or both?
What rule of thumb will you carry into the next mission?

post_reveal_facts.text: The guild's own earlier reports were later said to need correcting, and the guild's standing collapsed within weeks.
A royal commercial authority opened an inquiry after the decision day, not before it.
Later investigations attributed the troubles to hidden obligations and misleading statements; none of that was public when you committed.

later_events.text: The company acknowledged an SEC inquiry.
The company announced a formal SEC investigation.
The company said earlier reports would be restated, citing consolidation issues involving JEDI/Chewco and LJM1.
A merger with Dynegy was announced.
The company filed its third-quarter Form 10-Q.
Credit ratings fell below investment grade and Dynegy terminated the merger.
The company and certain subsidiaries sought Chapter 11 protection.
Investigations and enforcement actions described accounting manipulation, related-party arrangements and misleading disclosures.
